question.text: Chambal Managed Futures Fund is evaluating a domicile choice: onshore Mumbai (Cat III) vs GIFT-IFSC (Cat III). On an expected INR 100 crore annual business income from F&O, approximately how much in fund-level income-tax is saved in the holiday year by choosing GIFT-IFSC under Section 80LA (ignore surcharge/cess, use 42.744% vs 0%)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Applying the rates given in the stem (42.744% versus 0%), onshore Cat III fund-level tax on INR 100 crore of F&O business income = 100 × 42.744% = INR 42.744 crore, while a GIFT-IFSC Cat III claiming a 100% deduction under Section 80LA in a holiday year pays INR 0. The saving in the holiday year is therefore INR 42.744 crore, which rounds to INR 42.74 crore. The Trap: Options A (10 cr) and B (25 cr) understate the maximum marginal rate stack used in the stem. Option D (50 cr) exceeds the implied 42.744% rate. The key point is that Section 80LA, when claimed, takes the holiday-year liability to zero rather than to a lower rate. Note: Section 80LA, the 100% deduction, and the 0% holiday-year rate premise are not explicitly stated in the cited XIX-E (Category III AIF Managers) workbook pages, which generally note that IFSC set-up enjoys tax benefits. The arithmetic and 80LA framing above reflect the general Indian tax-law position on IFSC units rather than a workbook citation.
